_about: Own-words key points per USDA report, written on reading it (shown before the numbers the script takes from the report's tables). Key = GAIN report number, wmt-<market>-YYYY-MM or ers-<market>-YYYY-MM. Short, attributed numbers only.
EG2026-0003: Area seen up about a fifth to ~100,000 ha on Chinese and Indian demand for Egyptian ELS; freer seed-cotton auctions (no floor price) helped grower confidence.
IV2026-0005: Crop recovering from the jassid damage of the last two seasons; Post sees lint up ~4–5% to 590k bales, still below the 2024/25 level.
PK2026-0002: Post assumes average yields on similar area, so a slightly smaller crop; weak textile demand, with imports filling the gap. Post thinks 28–30% of last crop went unreported because of the tax regime.
IN2026-0020: First 2026/27 view: area +3% to 11.5m ha on trade-deal optimism and a normal-monsoon assumption; crop seen +7% at 25.2m bales with mill use rising.
MX2026-0023: Chihuahua growers returning to cotton lifts area ~12%; output still near historic lows, mill use flat against synthetics and Asian yarn.
SG2026-0002: Mali, Burkina Faso and Senegal together: area +8%, crop +27% as Mali recovers from jassids; doubt over whether Burkina's second ginner (SOCOMA) operates this season.
BG2026-0003: Energy shortages and fewer garment orders: Post cuts 2025/26 imports and use and sees 2026/27 imports lower at 7.7m bales.
BR2026-0019: High interest rates and costs push some area to corn: 2026/27 area and crop lower (18.0m bales), but Brazil stays the top exporter (15.0m).
VM2026-0009: Imports seen +10% to a record 8.4m bales on strong Chinese yarn demand; 2025/26 stocks cut to 913k bales.
CH2026-0054: Xinjiang subsidy changes push cotton off marginal land: crop seen −4.5% (7.2 Mt); imports only slightly above the low 2025/26 level; US cotton still faces an extra 10% tariff.
ID2026-0015: Struggling textile sector: imports seen lower in both 2025/26 and 2026/27 despite open trade.
UZ2026-0002: No PSD table in this report. Post cuts 2025/26 lint to ~750,000 t (from 906,000 t in its December 2025 report) and puts 2026/27 at ~780,000 t; Amu Darya flow at ~67% of normal is the main risk.
IN2026-0045: Below-normal Aug–Sep rain and a 12% monsoon deficit: Post cuts yield ~2% and the crop to 24.5m bales; planting 2% behind last year.
MX2026-0043: Good prices pull Chihuahua area up ~37%: crop raised to ~0.87m bales (+32% y/y); imports trimmed.
BR2026-0036: Slightly less area but record yields: crop only a little lower; strong end-season exports; stocks to fall, which Post sees as price-supportive.
PK2026-0011: Punjab area falls as cotton earns less than other crops: area 1.85m ha, crop cut to 4.9m bales, imports raised to 5.2m.
TU2026-0021: Smaller planting (275,000 ha) cuts the crop to ~2.27m bales; imports up to ~5.05m bales, with the US losing first place as supplier.
CH2026-0112: Xinjiang policy shrinks area and weather is less favourable: crop 7.12 Mt (−5.6% y/y). Post raises 2025/26 imports on trade data and the domestic/imported price gap.
SG2026-0004: Late rains delayed planting in all three countries and Mali got fertiliser late: area −4% and crop −7.7% versus the April report.
BG2026-0013: Policy support lifts 2026/27 imports; 2025/26 imports cut on high prices and freight. 2025/26 suppliers: Brazil 33%, India 15%, US 12%.
BR2026-0008: Market-development piece on Brazil's specialty coffee (credit, post-harvest and technical support are the constraints); no supply numbers.
GT2026-0003: Crop seen +3% (3.13m bags arabica); ~30% of hybrids are rust-tolerant; 81% of exports strictly hard bean; US takes 42%.
ES2026-0004: El Niño and rural labour shortages: 2026/27 seen down to 542k bags from 586k.
HO2026-0002: Better nutrition, pruning, new plantings and the on-year cycle: 2026/27 seen at 6.03m bags (5.53m in 2025/26), exports ~5.5m.
IN2026-0026: Wet Jan–Feb then a dry spell at flowering hit arabica yields; farmgate arabica −16% and robusta −11% since October but still above other origins.
MX2026-0026: Crop +1% on more robusta and better management; US is the main buyer.
ID2026-0021: Excess rain at flowering in south Sumatra and Java: crop −8% to 11.38m bags; 2025/26 arabica cut after floods in Aceh/North Sumatra.
KE2026-0011: Crop +12% to 950k bags on new area and better care after two years of high prices; new Coffee Act 2026 changes regulation.
CO2026-0008: Shift from La Niña to El Niño (drier) seen helping: crop +7.2% to 13.4m bags; lower prices encourage renovation.
CS2026-0004: Crop +3.5% to 1.2m bags, but strong colón, dearer fertiliser and El Niño limit the on-year gain.
ET2026-0005: Normal weather assumed: crop 12.1m bags, exports 7.13m; record cherry prices squeezed exporters in 2025/26.
NU2026-0003: El Niño risk and fertiliser +25%: crop seen 2.4m bags, ~8% below the 2.6m high.
PE2026-0008: Crop flat at 4.78m bags; US took 32% of exports.
UG2026-0001: More area after high prices: crop 7.2m bags (from 7.1m), exports 6.8m.
VM2026-0016: Planting after the 2024–25 price peak: crop up to 32.5m bags; lower prices are drawing stocks out to export.
BR2026-0025: Good weather in the main arabica areas: record crop after five weak years, exports seen +30%; exporters cautious on low stocks and El Niño risk to the end of harvest and to 2027/28.
BR2026-0040: El Niño brief: heat and dryness risk in central/northern Brazil (coffee flowering), excess rain in the south.
BR2026-0050: Record crop but heavy rain lowered arabica quality; exports picked up with the new crop after a slow first half; first flowering for 2027/28 looks good, El Niño watched.
ID2026-0044: Arabica cut again (logistics recovery in the highlands, warm dry mid-year); exports seen −7% to 7.3m bags.
IN2026-0062: Robusta +4% more than offsets arabica −9%; imports raised 20% to 1.67m bags as domestic supply tightens; exports raised 3%.
AS2026-0009: Full growing cycle after a short 2025/26 season: cane +8% to 30.7 Mt, sugar +9% to 4.18 Mt.
BR2026-0020: More cane but a bigger ethanol share (high gasoline prices make ethanol pay): sugar output and exports lower.
CH2026-0051: Guangxi cane lifts output: 2025/26 put 1.1 Mt above USDA's number; 2026/27 at 12.7 Mt, consumption flat at 15.8 Mt.
E42026-0032: Low prices cut beet sowing: 2026/27 output lower again, exports down, imports up.
ID2026-0014: Strong El Niño cuts cane area and yield: white sugar output down to 2.5 Mt, yet the government is expected to cut raw import allocations for industry.
PK2026-0005: Steady supply (~6.9 Mt): Post expects the government to allow ~300k t of exports.
TH2026-0011: Higher costs and weak markets: some northeast cane growers may switch crops; the sugar tax keeps domestic use flat.
MX2026-0025: Good rains and recovering area: output +1% to 5.45 Mt raw value; CONADESUCA has no official 2026/27 number yet.
IN2026-0024: Two good monsoons refilled groundwater: area and yields up, and output above consumption for the first time in two years.
RP2026-0013: El Niño and little new area: raw output lower; more refined imports under Sugar Order No. 2; no exports forecast.
CH2026-0125: Cane output up and demand flat: imports, including syrup and premix, seen lower as Beijing protects growers.
IN2026-0051: Erratic rain, waterlogging and pests cut yields and recovery: output now below consumption. Steepest price rise in 25 years led to duty-free raw imports, stock limits and an export ban; ending stocks fall sharply.
MX2026-0049: Output 5.70 Mt (+1%); the soda tax keeps demand flat; imports −32% after tariff increases; exports +42% as surplus is pushed out.
AS2026-0021: Dry since April: cane cut to 27.9 Mt (−1.8%), but high sugar content lifts sugar +4.4% to 4.0 Mt.
BR2026-0039: El Niño-linked irregular rain slows Centre-South crushing: some mills will crush into the off-season and cane will carry into 2027/28; North-Northeast near normal.
E42026-0076: Record-low beet area plus a severe summer drought: smallest EU crop since quotas ended; exports more than halve, imports rise, stocks drawn down.
PK2026-0013: Output unchanged at 6.91 Mt; with good stocks the export forecast goes up to 500k t.
RP2026-0032: Red-striped soft scale, El Niño and input costs: raw output forecast cut; no exports until the export policy is issued.
TH2026-0038: El Niño to cut cane yield and extraction; dry weather also threatens new plant cane for 2027/28. 2025/26 exports raised; more of 2026/27 exports to be refined as raws lose share to Brazil and Australia in Indonesia and Malaysia.
BR2026-0049: Wet September–October slowed the crush and cut TRS: cane 681 Mt (−2%), sugar 40.5 Mt (−4%), exports 31.7 Mt (−4.8%); mix kept at 49% sugar.
wmt-cotton-2026-11: Lead story: China sold ~1.9m bales from state reserves in Jul–Sep 2026 (about 60% US-origin), the first sales since 2023; USDA thinks ~13m bales remain and the trade expects the reserve to buy imports later in the season.

World 2026/27 revisions this month: production cut ~0.5m bales to 117.5m (India −0.5m to 23.5m; Australia +0.5m to 3.5m; China +0.5m to 34.0m); trade +0.1m to 44.8m; mill use −0.3m to 122.7m; ending stocks −0.1m to 70.6m.
US season-average farm price lowered 1¢ to 76¢/lb.
wmt-coffee-2026-07: World 2026/27 output seen at a record 189.7m bags (+10.8m), exports a record 131.4m; prices fell ~25% over the previous seven months as supply grew.
Brazil a record 71.9m bags (+8.9m): arabica +9.5m to 47.5m on near-record Minas yields, robusta −0.6m to 24.4m (cool, wet Espírito Santo); bean exports seen a record 45.0m.
wmt-sugar-2026-11: Lead story: China's deficit shrinks to ~2.4 Mt in 2025/26 (lowest in a decade) on output of ~12.9 Mt and weak demand; imports cut to ~4.2 Mt and 3.6 Mt in 2026/27; stocks rising toward 4.5 Mt while domestic prices fall and ICE No. 11 is up >20%.
World 2026/27: production 178.1 Mt (−5%), consumption 176.4 Mt (flat), exports 61.5 Mt (−5%), ending stocks 39.8 Mt (−12%, lowest since 2011/12).
India 29.5 Mt (−0.5 Mt), exports −13% to 3.1 Mt and stocks the lowest in 20 years; Brazil 40.5 Mt (−3 Mt) after heavy Centre-South rain, exports 31.7 Mt (−7%).
ers-cotton-2026-04: World 2025/26 crop 121.9m bales (+2%, highest since 2012/13); mill use raised 0.56m to 119.1m on China and India.
US 2025/26 stocks unchanged at 4.4m bales; Prospective Plantings put 2026 US area at ~9.6m acres (+4%).
ers-cotton-2026-05: First 2026/27 projections: world crop 116.0m bales (−6.6m) on lower yields, ending stocks 71.8m (−5.4m) as mill use rises.
US crop 13.3m bales, exports 12.3m; Brazil exports a record 15.0m.
ers-cotton-2026-06: World 2026/27 stocks 71.1m bales, lowest since 2018/19; mill use ~121.8m (+1.4%).
US 2025/26 exports raised 0.2m to 12.2m; 2026/27 US crop unchanged at 13.3m.
ers-cotton-2026-07: US 2026/27 crop raised 0.4m to 13.7m bales after June Acreage (9.85m acres); US stocks 4.1m (+0.4m).
World 2026/27 crop 117.3m, mill use ~122.0m (+1.7%); India's imports fall the most.
ers-cotton-2026-08: First survey-based US crop: 13.6m bales on ~10.5m planted acres.
World 2026/27 stocks 69.7m (−5.1m, lowest since 2011/12) as mill use (122.9m) exceeds production (117.6m) for the first time in 3 years; Australia's exports −21% to 4.5m.
ers-cotton-2026-09: US crop cut 0.4m to 13.2m bales on Southwest yields; US mill use trimmed.
World crop 117.3m (−4.6m y/y); trade 44.2m with Brazil 15.5m (35% share) and the US 12.3m (28%).
ers-cotton-2026-10: US crop raised 0.24m to 13.4m bales; Southwest abandonment ~34% and yield 517 lb/acre, lowest since 2003/04.
World 2026/27 stocks −5.0m y/y to the lowest since 2011/12; crop 118.0m, mill use 123.1m; India's imports −1.9m to 3.3m.
ers-sugar-2026-04: US 2025/26 beet sugar cut 33k STRV to 5.06m; deliveries for food raised 94k STRV on direct-consumption imports.
Mexico 2025/26 output raised 101k t to 5.125 Mt on better cane yield and recovery.
ers-sugar-2026-05: First US 2026/27 balance: supply 14.06m STRV; output 8.81m, lowest since 2019/20; imports set at minimum levels.
Mexico 2026/27 output 5.14 Mt (−0.7%) from Post's April Annual.
ers-sugar-2026-06: US 2026/27 production raised 254k STRV to 9.06m; 2025/26 deliveries raised 126k STRV.
Mexico 2026/27 output raised 141k t to 5.28 Mt after Post raised area and yield.
ers-sugar-2026-07: Multi-year SMD data revisions lower US 2026/27 beginning stocks and raise deliveries; 2025/26 deliveries +57k STRV.
Mexico 2025/26 output raised 74k t to 5.31 Mt on a strong finish; 2026/27 also raised.
ers-sugar-2026-08: US 2026/27 supply +169k STRV to 14.44m (higher stocks and imports); beet −30k and cane −23k STRV (Florida −123k).
Mexico 2025/26 output final at 5.325 Mt (+12% y/y).
ers-sugar-2026-09: US 2026/27 supply cut 168k STRV to 14.27m; cane −88k STRV (Florida 1.82m, lowest since 2013/14); imports −186k, mostly from Mexico (US Needs calculation).
ers-sugar-2026-10: US 2026/27 supply +119k STRV to 14.39m on larger beginning stocks; output −71k to 8.77m; food deliveries −50k; ending stocks +168k to 1.87m (stocks/use 14.9%).
Louisiana's early crop lifts 2025/26 cane sugar to a record 4.24m STRV.
